prompt_version: s5-extract-facts-v2 (adapted from Paleo Atlas extract-facts-v3; v2 after Sofía's S5 review)

facts.statement: The study analyzed single-cell RNA-sequencing data to look at HAX1 levels in normal lung tissue, primary lung cancer, advanced tumors, and metastases in lymph nodes and the brain.
facts.subject: cells_or_tissue

facts.statement: Researchers examined tissue samples from patients with lung adenocarcinoma to check the amount of HAX1 protein and how it related to patient health details.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Levels of HAX1 and the number of cells showing it were higher in lymph node and brain metastases than in the original primary tumors.
facts.subject: cells_or_tissue

facts.statement: In a group of 125 patients, high levels of HAX1 were linked to cancer spreading to lymph nodes, more advanced disease, and shorter survival times.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The genetic activity patterns linked to HAX1 focused on processes involving DNA copying and the cell cycle.
facts.subject: cells_or_tissue

facts.statement: Cancer cells that had spread to the brain also showed increased activity in mitochondrial functions and protein production.
facts.subject: cells_or_tissue

facts.statement: Higher HAX1 levels were associated with lower estimated numbers of B cells, T cells, and macrophages in the tumor environment.
facts.subject: cells_or_tissue

facts.statement: Reducing HAX1 in the lab made cancer cells less viable, slowed their division, and stopped tumors from growing in the mouse model.
facts.subject: animals
